subject.title: Migration-import config merge has no prototype-pollution guard, unlike the sibling config-path writer

question: Should OpenClaw harden the public migration config patch helper now by rejecting or skipping `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` keys across all migration-import config merges?
rationale: The source-reproducible issue is a security boundary concern in a public SDK helper, and maintainer/security review should choose the exact reject-vs-skip behavior before implementation.

options.title: Harden the SDK helper now
options.body: Add the existing blocked-key guard at the migration config merge/write boundary with focused regression tests for direct and Hermes-imported config patch values.

options.title: Handle in a coordinated security patch
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers group it with adjacent prototype-pollution hardening before publishing a fix.

options.title: Wait for deeper exploit proof
options.body: Leave the code unchanged until an end-to-end onboarding exploit path or second-order read is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Harden the SDK helper now
recommendation.body: Add the existing blocked-key guard at the migration config merge/write boundary with focused regression tests for direct and Hermes-imported config patch values.

likelyOwner.reason: The current migration helper, Hermes mapping, and onboarding import call site all trace to this recent implementation commit.
